OD-B13-S01.card: A friendly seafaring people sail the sleeping king home by night and leave him and his gifts on Ithaca's shore.

OD-B13-S02.card: Odysseus wakes in mist, does not recognize his own island, and fears he has been abandoned in a strange land.

OD-B13-S03.card: The goddess, disguised as a shepherd, tells him he is home; he lies about who he is, and she reveals herself.

OD-B13-S04.card: Athena helps him hide his treasure in a cave and plan against the suitors; first he must go to his swineherd.

OD-B13-S05.card: The goddess turns the king into a ragged old beggar so he can test his household without being recognized.

OD-B14-S01.card: Fierce dogs attack the disguised king at the swineherd's farm until Eumaeus drives them off and welcomes the stranger.

OD-B14-S02.card: The swineherd curses the suitors eating his master's herds; the beggar swears Odysseus will return, but Eumaeus will not believe it.

OD-B14-S03.card: The disguised king tells a long invented life story, testing how much the swineherd will believe.

OD-B14-S04.card: On a cold night, the beggar hints with a story that he needs a cloak, and the swineherd generously lends one.

OD-B15-S01.card: In Sparta, the goddess warns the king's son to sail home at once and avoid the suitors' ambush.

OD-B15-S02.card: The son leaves the king and queen of Sparta with gifts; a bird sign suggests his father's revenge is near.

OD-B15-S03.card: At the harbor, the son takes aboard a fugitive prophet and sails through the night toward Ithaca.

OD-B15-S04.card: At the hut, the swineherd tells the beggar how he was kidnapped as a child and raised in Odysseus's family.

OD-B15-S05.card: A hawk kills a dove, which the prophet reads as good news; the son lands secretly and walks toward the swineherd's farm.

OD-B16-S01.card: The son reaches the hut; the swineherd weeps with joy, and the disguised father offers his seat.

OD-B16-S02.card: The swineherd leaves to tell the queen her son is safe, and the goddess signals Odysseus that he may reveal himself.

OD-B16-S03.card: Restored to his true form, Odysseus tells his son who he is; after doubt, they embrace and weep.

OD-B16-S04.card: Father and son count the suitors and plan to hide the palace weapons, telling no one, not even the queen.

OD-B16-S05.card: The suitors learn the son escaped their ambush; Antinous urges murder, and the queen confronts them.

OD-B16-S06.card: The goddess makes Odysseus a beggar again before the swineherd returns, and father and son keep their secret.

OD-B17-S01.card: The son returns to the palace and greets his mother but hides his father's return; the prophet says Odysseus is already here.

OD-B17-S02.card: On the road to town, a goatherd who serves the suitors kicks and insults the beggar, who holds back his anger.

OD-B17-S03.card: Odysseus's old dog, neglected for twenty years, recognizes his master's voice, wags his tail, and dies.

OD-B17-S04.card: The disguised king enters his own hall and begs from each suitor to learn which of them are decent.

OD-B17-S05.card: Antinous insults the beggar and hits him with a footstool, breaking the rule that strangers must be protected.

OD-B17-S06.card: The queen asks to meet the stranger; he waits until evening, and her son's sneeze seems to promise the suitors' deaths.

OD-B17-S07.card: The swineherd returns to his farm, leaving the disguised king alone in the palace among the suitors.

OD-B18-S01.card: A local beggar tries to chase Odysseus from the door, and the amused suitors push the two into a fight.

OD-B18-S02.card: Odysseus reveals his strength and knocks the other beggar down with one blow, careful not to kill him.

OD-B18-S03.card: The beggar warns the kindest suitor that the king will soon return; Amphinomus is shaken but stays.

OD-B18-S04.card: The queen appears before the suitors and shames them into bringing her gifts, while her disguised husband silently admires her cleverness.

OD-B18-S05.card: A disloyal maid and Eurymachus mock the beggar; Eurymachus throws a stool, and the son ends the night.

OD-B19-S01.card: Father and son secretly carry the weapons out of the hall, leaving the suitors unarmed for what is coming.

OD-B19-S02.card: The queen questions the beggar, tells how she has stalled the suitors for years, and asks proof that he knew her husband.

OD-B19-S03.card: The beggar describes her husband's clothes exactly; she weeps, while he hides his own grief and promises Odysseus is near.

OD-B19-S04.card: Washing the beggar's feet, the old nurse feels a childhood scar and knows him; he forces her to stay silent.

OD-B19-S05.card: A memory: young Odysseus is gored by a wild boar while hunting, which left the scar the nurse just found.

OD-B19-S06.card: The queen tells a dream of an eagle killing geese, then announces a contest: she will marry whoever masters Odysseus's bow.

OD-B20-S01.card: Odysseus lies awake, angry and doubtful, until the goddess promises to protect him; upstairs the queen dreams of her husband.

OD-B20-S02.card: Odysseus asks the gods for a sign; thunder sounds from a clear sky, and a tired servant prays for the suitors' end.

OD-B20-S03.card: Herdsmen arrive for a festival: the goatherd insults the beggar, but a loyal cowherd greets him warmly.

OD-B20-S04.card: A suitor throws an ox hoof at the beggar; the son warns he will kill the next man who attacks his guest.

OD-B20-S05.card: The suitors laugh wildly while the prophet sees them covered in blood and shadow, and warns they are doomed.

OD-B21-S01.card: The queen takes her husband's great bow from the storeroom, weeps over it, and brings it to the suitors.

OD-B21-S02.card: The queen announces the contest; her son nearly strings the bow himself, until his father signals him to stop.

OD-B21-S03.card: One suitor after another fails to bend the bow, and the shamed suitors postpone the contest.

OD-B21-S04.card: Outside, Odysseus shows his scar to the two loyal herdsmen, reveals who he is, and gives them their tasks.

OD-B21-S05.card: The beggar asks to try the bow; the suitors rage, the son sends his mother upstairs, and the swineherd delivers it.

OD-B21-S06.card: The nurse locks the women away and the cowherd ties the gate shut, sealing the suitors inside.

OD-B21-S07.card: The beggar strings the bow with ease and shoots an arrow through all twelve axes; his son arms and joins him.

OD-B22-S01.card: Odysseus throws off his rags, shoots the cruelest suitor, and announces who he is to the stunned, unarmed men.

OD-B22-S02.card: A suitor leader offers to repay everything; Odysseus refuses and kills him, and his son spears another attacker.

OD-B22-S03.card: The son brings armor and spears for his father and the herdsmen, but leaves the storeroom door open.

OD-B22-S04.card: The traitor goatherd sneaks weapons to the suitors through the open door; the herdsmen catch him and tie him up.

OD-B22-S05.card: The goddess, disguised as an old friend, turns aside the suitors' spears and fills them with terror.

OD-B22-S06.card: The last suitors are killed; Odysseus spares the singer and the herald, whom his son says were forced to serve.

OD-B22-S07.card: The nurse names twelve maids who sided with the suitors; they clean the hall and are hanged, and the goatherd killed.

OD-B22-S08.card: Odysseus purifies the hall with fire; loyal servants embrace him, and the nurse goes to wake the queen.

OD-B23-S01.card: The old nurse tells the queen her husband is home and has killed the suitors; she cannot believe it.

OD-B23-S02.card: The queen sits facing the stranger in silence; their son scolds her, and Odysseus has the house prepare a cover story.

OD-B23-S03.card: Music and dancing make neighbors think a wedding is happening, hiding the killings; the queen still holds back.

OD-B23-S04.card: The queen orders their bed moved; he protests he built it around a living tree, their private secret, and she embraces him.

OD-B23-S05.card: In bed, husband and wife tell each other their years apart; he admits one last journey still awaits him.

OD-B23-S06.card: At dawn the king, his son, and the herdsmen arm themselves and slip out of town to reach his father's farm.

OD-B24-S01.card: The god who guides the dead leads the suitors' spirits to the underworld, where great warriors of the past wait.

OD-B24-S02.card: Among the dead, a suitor tells how Odysseus returned and killed them, and the spirits praise the queen's faithfulness.

OD-B24-S03.card: Odysseus finds his grieving father working alone in an orchard, tests him with a lie, then cannot help revealing himself.

OD-B24-S04.card: He proves himself with his scar and the trees his father gave him as a boy; the old man collapses in joy.

OD-B24-S05.card: The father is bathed and made strong again, and the farm household feasts, while news of the killings spreads through town.

OD-B24-S06.card: In town, the suitors' families mourn; Eupithes ignores warnings and leads armed relatives toward the farm for revenge.

OD-B24-S07.card: The goddess asks the king of the gods whether to allow war or peace; Zeus decides Odysseus stays king and peace returns.

OD-B24-S08.card: The relatives attack; the old father kills their leader with a spear, and the fighting threatens to become another slaughter.

OD-B24-S09.card: The goddess commands both sides to stop, Zeus sends a thunderbolt, and she binds king and people in a lasting peace.
